Thunderous cheers and Sophie Ellis-Bextor’s disco hit Murder on the Dancefloor blasted across Adelaide 36ers Arena, as the Thunderbirds booked a spot in the Super Netball grand final.

The hometown heroes secured a 14-point victory against the Melbourne Vixens – who will need to win the preliminary final next week to keep alive their back-to-back premiership dream.

The Vixens will host West Coast Fever at John Cain Arena in the preliminary final next week, after the Perth team knocked out the Melbourne Mavericks in a thrilling finish.

The Vixens had a strong start, but the clinical Thunderbirds – aided by superb performances from goal shooter Elmere van der Berg and defender Shamera-Sterling Humphrey – were too good.

Sterling-Humphrey performed brilliantly with some exceptional intercepts and defence in the second quarter. With mere seconds on the clock, the ball sailed towards goal shooter Sophie Garbin, but Sterling- Humphrey had other ideas.

The defender channelled her inner AFL star and launched herself on top of Garbin to intercept the ball, almost somersaulting over to stop the goal.

After the game, Sterling-Humphrey, who has previously posted about the difficulties she experienced after the birth of her first child, said she wants to prioritise her mental health in the week off before the grand final.

“We get together as a team and we are going to go bowling, for me, it’s taking care of my mental health because I’m still going through postpartum depression,” she said.

When asked how she was going, the star defender said: “I would say I’m OK.”

“But there are days … the entire week in was in depression mode, and netball keeps me happy,” she said.

While the Thunderbirds have a week off, the Vixens will prepare for their showdown against the Fever, who won in front of a roaring green crowd at RAC Arena.

The Mavericks had a strong start and snatched momentum for the first quarter, but Fever hit back with a nine-goal turnaround in the second. A turning point in the game happened in the final few minutes when a pesky bee briefly threatened to interrupt play.

The insect flew around players’ faces, but it didn’t seem to bother Fever’s goal shooter Sasha Glasgow, who expertly slotted a super shot to level scores.

The Fever took control of the game in the second half and led by 10 goals at one point in the final quarter. But the Mavericks rallied in the dying minutes, reducing the margin to just four-goals.

The Mavericks fumbled super shot opportunities and the Fever capitalised on the rebound to hold on and win.

Mavericks captain Amy Parmenter said she was incredibly proud of the group.

“We put our heart and soul into that last five minutes,” she said.

Thanks so much for joining us.

The Adelaide Thunderbirds have booked a spot in the Super Netball Grand Final, but who will join them?

Melbourne Vixens and West Coast Fever will face each other in a prelim final next week at John Cain Arena, Saturday, June 27 at 7.30pm.

See you then!

In the dying minutes of the final quarter, the Melbourne Mavericks looked like they were on the cusp of an extraordinary victory.

The team were 10 goals down but fought back to reduce the margin to four points, and had an opportunity to get ahead with supershots. However, the visitors fumbled and missed crucial opportunities.

West Coast Fever capitalised on the rebounds and won by four goals, booking a prelim final against the Melbourne Vixens at John Cain Arena.

Melbourne Mavericks captain Amy Parmenter said the loss “definitely hurt right now”.

“We put our heart and soul into that last five minutes,” she said.

Final score:West Coast Fever wins 56-52

The Mavs have just missed two Super shots. Their game is over with mere seconds to go, a comeback is now impossible.

We’ve got less than two minutes and the margin is down to three points. Fever look stunned.

Can the Perth side hold on or can Melbourne launch a comeback?

Mavericks head coach Gerard Murphy called a tactical timeout. Can the Melbourne visitors launch an insane comeback?

They look a bit flat, but captain Amy Parmenter lifts the team with a rallying cry.

Moments later, Uneeq Palavi takes a super shot. Suddenly, the margin is back to five-points.

Can they do it?

The Fever are running on top of the Mavericks.

They’ve scored the last seven goals and have capitalised on some shaky moments from the Melbourne visitors.

The Mavericks are running out of time and will need to do something extraordinary,

Score: Fever lead 54-44

The Mavericks desperately need to find their groove and clinch a critical comeback.

But Fever have opened with a bang and lead the final quarter by eight goals. The home team have all the momentum and have put their foot down.

The Fever have extensive finals experience and it’s showing.

Score: Fever lead 50-42

We’ve got fifteen minutes of play left and it’s still anyone’s game.

The Mavericks had an opportunity to score a critical super shot in the final 30 seconds of the game but fumbled, sending the ball out.

Fever converted the turnover to clinch a four-point lead.
